correctness.rationale: The branch from V_i maps affinely onto (0,λ^(i−2)], so uniform conditional measure on a target cell persists after every specified itinerary. The cell increment is R−1 with P(R=r)=(1−λ)λ^r on r≥0. Put a=z(1−λ), c=aλ. Subtract λ times each next-state equation from the previous one to obtain f_i−λf_(i+1)=af_(i−1) below the top, and (1−c)f_(m−1)=af_(m−2) at the top. Starting there and working backwards to f_4=1 gives exactly H_m=aP_(m−6)/P_(m−5). Positivity follows from P_j=(r_+^(j+2)−r_-^(j+2))/(r_+−r_-), with r±=(1±√(1−4c))/2 and positive repeated-root limit. At m=6 this is the geometric one-state formula; z=0 gives zero. The skip-free first-hit sequences have total increment −1, so the cyclic lemma on weak compositions gives the Catalan coefficient and the square-root PGF. At z=1, the roots are λ and 1−λ (or repeated at 1/2), and 1−H_m(1) is exactly the stated height tail with exponent m−3. A finite strip is left almost surely by the positive-probability all-down run, so treating nonreturns as infinite height does not alter this computation. The unrestricted PGF at one gives the stated missing mass. For the duration scaling at λ=1/2±ε, Stirling gives prefactor 1/(2√π) and exponential factor (1−4ε²)^(n−1); the bound by a constant times n^(−3/2)e^(−4nε²) justifies the tail integral. The supercritical mass adds 4 after division by ε. q=1∓4ε+O(ε²) gives the two stated depth limits. The result is confined to the auxiliary map, with no transfer by semiconjugacy.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Setting i=1 in the boundary solution gives G_1=s(1−λ)(r_+^(B−1)−r_-^(B−1))/(r_+^B−r_-^B). Multiply by √z and take s=√z and B=m−3: the ratio is precisely P_(m−6)/P_(m−5). This reduces the exact claimed joint formula to the older side-specific formula by the Bernoulli runs, not by separately fitting marginals. The scaling then needs only Stirling summation of the Catalan law and substitution into the geometric height law.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Shift the cell index by four, start the Bernoulli walk at 1, and replace each R−1 step by R independent-success up steps of probability λ followed by one down step of probability 1−λ. The geometric run lengths between downs are iid with the prescribed law. Each run peaks exactly one unit above its post-down value. Therefore on returns keeping pre-return cells below m is exactly not hitting B=m−3 before zero in the expanded walk. A successful return has τ downs and τ−1 ups, so its expanded duration is 2τ−1. This bijective time and barrier conversion gives H_m(z)=√z G_1(√z), where G_i(s)=E_i[s^T; T_0<T_B] and T is the classical absorption time.

value.rationale: Duration and maximum cell depth are well motivated, but the Bernoulli run representation turns the joint law into the classical finite-barrier ruin statistic with a deterministic clock change on returns. The given formula and separate near-critical limits add no independently unresolved invariant after this identification. The record deliberately claims no extension to original bimodal-map return times or a new joint critical limit beyond the finite transform and its marginal consequences.
residual_risks: The classical comparison is still a useful explanation of the auxiliary map's law; lack of a distinct contribution does not imply the formulas are wrong or useless.
